J01.note: Both states lead with the status and the object being minted (artwork, The Memes #547, full title, quantity 3, recipient); the collector always knows what is happening and to what.

J02.note: Status heading, then artwork and title, then quantity/recipient details, then help or explorer link; the same order carries across both stages so the lifecycle reads as one flow.

J03.note: Heading and artwork dominate; labels are muted, the recovery disclosure and the explorer link recede as secondary.

J04.note: Dark iron surface, rounded-xl card, small rounded artwork thumbnail, primary-tinted spinner, mono reserved for the address, no celebration or hype; the darker 15px edge strips at 1440 look like a harness/scrollbar-gutter artifact and were not charged.

J05.note: Compact modal with related facts grouped under one divider; no filler.

J06.note: Consistent label/value roles and a well-wrapped title, but the disclosure uses the browser-default triangle marker and the desktop subtitle leaves 'confirming.' alone on its second line.

J07.note: Plain, specific operational copy: 'Confirm in your wallet', 'Mint submitted', 'Waiting for network confirmation.', 'View transaction'; no brief leakage or abstraction.

J09.note: Both pinned states are deliberate and distinct, with wallet recovery guidance and an explorer fallback; the confirm state shows no visible way to cancel (disclosure contents and dismissal behavior were not observed).

J10.note: At 390 the card keeps a 16px gutter, the title wraps to three lines cleanly, the full address fits on one line, and the disclosure row is a full-width touch target; no overflow.

J13.note: Lifecycle is clear (confirm in wallet, then submitted kept distinct from confirmed), no timing promises, explorer link secondary, wallet recovery offered; the confirm state names no amount to check against the wallet prompt and the recipient is bare hex with no 'your wallet' cue.

findings.observation: The modal tells the user to 'Review the mint details and network fee before confirming' but lists only quantity and recipient; no mint price or total appears.
findings.consequence: A newcomer looking at the wallet prompt has no amount in the 6529 UI to compare the wallet's ETH value against while the mint form is hidden behind the modal.
findings.change: Add a 'Total' row under Quantity showing the real quantity × unit price in ETH followed by '+ network fee' (message-backed), using the same price data the mint form already shows.
findings.acceptance_check: confirm_wallet shows a Total row in ETH that equals quantity × the form's unit price, marked '+ network fee', fitting on one line at 390x844 and 1440x900.

findings.observation: Recipient is shown only as a 42-character hex address with no indication whether it is the connected wallet, a delegate, or another address.
findings.consequence: A person new to wallets cannot tell at a glance that the cards will arrive in their own wallet.
findings.change: When the recipient is the connected wallet, add a short qualifier such as 'Your connected wallet' (or the profile handle/ENS) above the address, keeping the full address below.
findings.acceptance_check: When minting to the connected wallet, both states identify the recipient as the user's wallet or profile in words while still showing the full address.

findings.observation: The confirm state has no close control and no visible line explaining how to back out; only the collapsed 'Wallet not showing?' disclosure is offered.
findings.consequence: A user who changes their mind may not know that rejecting in the wallet cancels the mint and may feel trapped behind the modal.
findings.change: Add one muted line, e.g. 'To cancel, reject the request in your wallet.', or a visible Cancel/close control if the flow supports dismissal at this stage.
findings.acceptance_check: The confirm_wallet state shows, without expanding the disclosure, how to cancel the mint.

findings.observation: 'Wallet not showing?' uses the browser-default filled triangle marker, unlike the outlined icon set in the heading; the subtitle wraps so 'confirming.' sits alone on its second line at 1440.
findings.consequence: Small finish inconsistencies in an otherwise tight modal.
findings.change: Replace the native details marker with the repo's chevron icon (rotating on open) and balance the subtitle wrap (e.g. text-wrap: balance or a slightly wider measure).
findings.acceptance_check: The disclosure marker matches the repo icon set and the desktop subtitle no longer leaves a single-word last line.

preserve: Artwork thumbnail with 'The Memes #547' and the full card title in both stages
Quantity and recipient carried unchanged from confirm_wallet into submitted
'Mint submitted' with a spinner and 'Waiting for network confirmation.' kept distinct from confirmed; no celebration before confirmation
'This window updates automatically.' with no invented timing promise
'View transaction' explorer link as a secondary text link only after submission
Collapsed 'Wallet not showing?' recovery disclosure in the confirm state
Plain operational copy with no hype, jargon, or brief leakage
Dark iron card with rounded-xl frame, mono used only for the address
390px layout: 16px gutters, cleanly wrapping title, full address on one line, full-width disclosure target
